set.body:
GiftiSurfaceCodec.transformMatrix takes pointSet.transforms.headOption and hands it to SurfaceGeometry.surfaceToWorld regardless of DataSpace/TransformedSpace, so a mesh whose first CoordinateSystemTransformMatrix goes into NIFTI_XFORM_UNKNOWN (or Talairach, or a second matrix into scanner space that comes later) is treated as if it placed the mesh in world coordinates. A GIFTI may carry several transforms and the useful one is not always the first.

Asked for: select the transform whose TransformedSpace is one the caller can place (NIFTI_XFORM_SCANNER_ANAT, ALIGNED_ANAT, TALAIRACH, MNI_152), expose the chosen transform's DataSpace/TransformedSpace on the result (or expose the full Vector[GiftiTransform] to the caller), and make an unplaceable non-identity transform an explicit error rather than a silent surfaceToWorld.

Neuropublish implements this selection itself in backend Derivation.worldGeometry (branch stage5/rendition-review-fixes): it applies the chosen matrix to the positions, writes world positions in the rendition, keeps the matrix as sourceTransform provenance, and refuses a non-identity transform into an unknown space. If ScalaFIM takes the selection, neuropublish would drop its copy.

Filed from neuropublish branch stage5/rendition-review-fixes.

Sequential assessment 2026-09-12:
Confirmed at current GiftiSurfaceCodec.transformMatrix: transforms.headOption is converted into surfaceToWorld without inspecting either declared space. Retain P1 core-correctness. The original proposed selection is insufficient: choosing the first transform into any recognized space merely replaces one order-dependent rule with another. Scanner, aligned, Talairach and MNI targets are not interchangeable, and a generic scanner-space code alone is not subject/frame registration evidence.

Already implemented: the raw GiftiDataArray exposes the full Vector[GiftiTransform], including optional dataSpace/transformedSpace and finite 16-element matrix values. Do not duplicate that raw-model feature. The geometry-only reader return loses the selected transform provenance and has no caller target-selection contract.

Refined acceptance:
1. Define an explicit caller-owned placement/target selection contract at the surface reader boundary, using existing frame/affine types where applicable. Do not silently prioritize scanner versus MNI versus Talairach.
2. Make ambiguous eligible transforms an explicit error unless the caller explicitly selects one. Permuting the document's transforms must not silently change geometry for the same declared target. Cover two transforms into the same target with different matrices.
3. Preserve the chosen DataSpace, TransformedSpace and original matrix with the decoded result; callers using convenience geometry-only APIs need a documented safe default/error policy. Do not claim generic space codes establish correspondence to an arbitrary image.
4. Distinguish native/unplaced coordinates from world placement. Unknown/missing-space and no-transform cases require an explicit contract; an identity matrix is not by itself evidence of a world frame. Reject unknown non-identity placement and malformed/non-affine matrices explicitly.
5. Verify on JVM and JS through public readers with independent landmarks, reordered transforms, multiple eligible targets, unknown/absent spaces and retained provenance. Preserve coordinate precision and avoid double-applying the selected matrix.
6. Bound the change to ScalaFIM surface decoding/placement. Any removal of Neuropublish's selection implementation requires separate downstream qualification.

Assessment only: no transform-selection repair or current geometry correctness is claimed by this note.
set.title: GIFTI: make surface transform selection explicit and preserve coordinate-space provenance
